label: token right after an early l (l at position 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires during the original phase on the step right after the input l, but only when that l is original token 0 or 1 (so t = 1 or t = 2). It does not depend on the current token. Magnitude depends on position: it is strongest (about 0.95-1.0 of max) at t=1 when the sequence starts with l, and weaker (about 0.6-0.8) at t=2 when l is the second token. It does not fire after an l later in the sequence (t >= 3 gives only a few weak activations), and it never fires at the delimiter or during the copy phase. The only misses are about 5k near-zero activations at t=1 after a first token of a or k (0.2% of activation mass). On dev the predicate has precision 1.0 and mass recall 0.998.

issues: Minor inaccuracy in the explanation: it says the only misses are near-zero activations at t=1 after a first token of a or k. On test, (phase==0)&(t==1)&(prev_tok in {a,k}) accounts for about 4,470 of the 5,345 missed steps, with mass recall about 3e-6. The other roughly 870 misses are weak activations at t=3 after an l, all in the bottom activation quartile, with mass recall 0.0016. The explanation does mention those weak t>=3 activations elsewhere, so this does not change the verdict.

The other claims hold. Copy phase has 2 active steps out of 2.7M and the delimiter has 0. t=0 has 0 active steps and t>=4 has only 2. The magnitude claim checks out: t=1 after l covers 72-100% of the top two activation quartiles, and t=2 after l mostly covers quartiles 1-3 and 0% of the top quartile. On test the predicate has precision 1.0 with 0 false positives, F1 0.926 and mass recall 0.998.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate. Adding t=3 after l lowers precision (0.054 for that slice alone), and adding t=1 after a/k drops F1 to 0.72. No better predicate found.
